relatedKnowledge.title: Related PHI OS knowledge
relatedKnowledge.description: When reality is treated as a collection of already completed objects, the first question is usually what those objects are. Looking backward through formation produces a different sequence of questions. How did distinguishable states appear? Why were some relations preserved while others disappeared? How did regions, boundaries, networks, and positions become possible?

relatedKnowledge.title: Related PHI OS knowledge
relatedKnowledge.description: The movement from Difference to navigation is not one jump. It is a chain in which reality becomes progressively more readable. Difference makes comparison possible. Constraint selects realizable paths. Structure preserves relational patterns. Structural differences form regions and networks. Only then do stable references exist from which position and direction can be read. Navigation is therefore not an extra function added at the end. It depends on the structures created by every earlier layer.
